title: Temptation and Sin
definition: Temptation and sin describe the enticement toward evil and the sinful choice to distrust and disobey God.
summary: Temptation invites people toward sin, but God calls His people to resist and obey.
christFocus: Jesus was tempted without sin and gives mercy and help to those who are tempted.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Temptation often presents sin as desirable, reasonable, or necessary. It questions God's goodness, twists desire, and promises satisfaction apart from obedience.

Sin occurs when the heart yields to what God forbids or refuses what God commands. Temptation may come from the flesh, the world, or the devil, but each person remains responsible before God.

Christ gives real hope in temptation. He resisted perfectly, sympathizes with weakness, and provides mercy, escape, and power for obedience.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people are confused about the difference between being tempted and giving in to sin. This doctrine matters because it helps believers resist early, confess honestly, and find help in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Learn your patterns of temptation and respond quickly. Use Scripture, prayer, accountability, and practical boundaries. When you sin, confess and return to Christ rather than hiding in shame.
